{"id":"PKIX-vbyn","title":"pkix-dane-resolver: debian.org TLSA returns Indeterminate under hickory despite being signed","description":"## Observed

Through one HickoryTlsaResolver built on pkix_dnssec_anchor::CURRENT with UpstreamConfig::Servers([9.9.9.9:53]), AsyncTlsaResolver::resolve reports:

  443 good.dane.huque.com  -> Ok((Secure, 1))
  25  mail.huque.com       -> Ok((Secure, 3))
  25  mx1.freebsd.org      -> Ok((Secure, 1))
  25  mailly.debian.org    -> Ok((Indeterminate, 2))   <-- records present, status wrong

The records come back. Only the DNSSEC status differs.

## Why this looks like a real problem rather than a quirk of that zone

- debian.org has a DS record in the parent: 40756 8 2 BBE42151B1..., algorithm 8 is RSA/SHA-256, which hickory supports.
- 9.9.9.9 sets AD on the answer, so the upstream validated it.
- Three other signed zones validate Secure through the same resolver, anchors and upstream in the same process, so this is not an environment or anchor problem.

So a domain that is signed, validated by its upstream, and using a supported algorithm comes back as unvalidatable. Something between hickory and that zone disagrees.

## Why it matters

Indeterminate folds into "insecure" for every consumer of this crate. Under RFC 7672 that means DANE silently does not apply to debian.org mail -- exactly the quiet failure the DANE work has been trying to avoid everywhere else. Under an opportunistic TLS policy nothing reports an error; DANE just stops happening.

If the cause is general rather than specific to that zone, the blast radius is every domain sharing whatever property triggers it.

## Not introduced by the SMTP driver

Found while writing the live tests for PKIX-rgc6, and checked against resolve() directly before blaming the new code. The SMTP discovery driver reports Indeterminate because resolve() does. The live test uses freebsd.org instead, with a comment pointing here.

## Where to look

1. Whether the TLSA RRset at _25._tcp.mailly.debian.org has an RRSIG at all, or whether the signature is there and hickory rejects it. dig +dnssec against the authoritative servers rather than a recursive resolver, so a recursor is not answering from cache with the crypto stripped.
2. Whether debian.org delegates _tcp or mailly as a separate zone with its own (possibly unsigned) delegation. An unsigned delegation inside a signed parent is a legitimate Insecure, and if so the right answer is Insecure rather than Indeterminate -- which is itself informative, since this crate currently cannot tell those apart in a negative or partially-signed case.
3. Whether this is the same gap as the authenticated-denial follow-up already noted in classify_lookup_error, where the negative answer DNSSEC state is not surfaced per-record.
4. hickory issue tracker for known validation gaps on NSEC3 opt-out or specific signer configurations.

## Acceptance

[ ] Cause identified: hickory bug, zone configuration, or a correct Insecure being mislabelled Indeterminate
[ ] If hickory: upstream issue filed and linked, with a note on whether a workaround exists
[ ] If the zone: recorded, and the live test comment in smtp_discovery.rs corrected to say so
[ ] If Indeterminate is wrong for a legitimately-unsigned delegation, decide whether this crate should distinguish that case","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T00:40:27.247252285Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T00:40:27.247252285Z"}
